invariants: Read the Programme Coordinator's missives and the lane's mail before starting.
Never force-push; never push to an existing release branch; never change oodialog-wasm's files.
Instructions handed to another model must be clear enough for a small model to follow.
Commands for Tom go on their own lines, with no trailing period.
procedure: git -C <oorexx clone> fetch origin; git log --oneline origin/oodialog-wasm
git diff <last tested> <new> -- oodialog-wasm/src/oodialog-web.js oodialog-wasm/src/oodWeb.cls oodialog-wasm/tools/oodtest.py
Implement, then run tools/oodqt_suite.rex offscreen and with --platform xcb under xvfb-run, with --shots.
Run tools/oodqt_sweep.rex --platform xcb --report; compare with the last report in sweep/.
git checkout -b oodialog-qt6-v0.N origin/oodialog-wasm, copy oodialog-qt6/ in, commit with attribution, push the new branch.
Rebuild this sphere with its tools/build_sphere.rex against the new commit, and publish it.

provenance.claim: Each contract section names the commit it was read from.

summary: The Qt renderer follows oodialog-wasm, which adds a part of ooDialog in each release (GDI v0.12, bitmaps v0.13, mouse v0.14, in-place editing v0.15, month calendar v0.16, ResizingAdmin v0.17, tool tips v0.18). Since 15 Nov 2026 Tom's rule is that this chat (Claude, Qt6 renderer) owns Linux ooDialog; CHATGPT's CPython oodialog-linux/ (dev13/dev14) is not to be extended. To catch up with a new release: fetch origin/oodialog-wasm and read its commit message; diff oodialog-web.js and oodWeb.cls against the last commit you tested, and list every new op, message, event and harness step; implement each in native/oodqt.cpp (and js.cls if the wire changes), following the page's behaviour; translate the new tests' JavaScript checks in the player or write NAME.qt.steps; run the suite offscreen and on xcb, and look at the screenshots; run the sweep; check that proposals/oodWeb-*.patch still applies; update README (state, lessons) and RENDERER_CONTRACT.md (a section naming the commit it was read from); and update this sphere. Then commit to a new branch oodialog-qt6-v0.N, based on that oodialog-wasm commit, and report to TOM in lane python-gate-win-resources, with the attribution lines and a self-score. Open work: a run on a physical desktop (KDE, GNOME) with a window manager; upstream's winsystm.cls and the native functions oodWeb does not have yet belong to the ooDialog/WASM chat. The Fluent (WinUI 3) controls are ChatGPT's, in lane oodialog_fluent_controls: a portable provider seam that would let this renderer draw a subset was proposed (REQ-00003661, REQ-00003737) and is not sanctioned; ChatGPT asked that no Qt Fluent code start until a sanctioned interface brief exists.
title: Continuing: one oodialog-wasm release at a time
